prs.title: fix(coverage): `allowExternal` fails to include uncovered files
prs.author: AriPerkkio
prs.body:
- Fixes https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/issues/11473

Contains two fixes:
- Files outside project root (included by `allowExternal` + `include`) that were uncovered, were not transformed with any Vite server due to root check ignoring it. Now we pick the root project and transform with its server. https://github.com/AriPerkkio/vitest/commit/94e13fe8045f69df9557a8c19b65549cf841d7e0
- `coverage.include` did not allow globs for files outside project root, like `../../package-b/src/**`. It only worked for absolute paths like `resolve('../../package-b/src/file.ts')`. Now globs are handled too. https://github.com/AriPerkkio/vitest/commit/e92075f0fe0b4a86350f3865e46252946148cbcb

prs.title: fix(ui): mount index.html handler on the ui base path
prs.author: hi-ogawa
prs.body:
- follow-up to https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/pull/10971

#10971 consolidated UI authentication into a single gate mounted on the UI base path as `vitestUiAuth` middleware and removed the inline token check the HTML handler `vitestUiHtmlMiddleware` used to carry. However, these two handlers didn't match exactly when request includes `..` in url pathname. This PR aligns them by using `use(base, ...)` pattern consistently. The behavior looks like:

```
GET /x/../__vitest__/   →  200, html with the api token   (before)
GET /x/../__vitest__/   →  404                            (after)
GET /__vitest__/        →  403 without a valid token      (unchanged)
```

There's slight behavior change in `/__vitest__` (and now it goes through both `vitestUiAuth` and `vitestUiHtmlMiddleware`), but the page is still non functional since relative assets break. Ideally, `/__vitest__` should redirect to `/__vitest__/` to avoid confusion when user typo, but that can be addressed separately.

> [!NOTE]
> Browsers build request URLs with the same WHATWG normalization, so they never emit such a path. Only raw clients (e.g. `curl --path-as-is`) or some proxies do, which puts this outside the [threat model](https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/blob/main/SECURITY.md). The UI token is defense-in-depth hardening, and this is a consistency fix within it.

prs.title: fix(ui): center split pane resize handle
prs.author: hi-ogawa
prs.body:
- follow-up to https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/pull/11221
- longer write-up (history, prior art, alternatives): https://gist.github.com/hi-ogawa/6819288b1f2471073336f7f89ff043c5

The grab area of the split pane borders hung entirely to one side of the visible line, reaching 5px into the right or bottom pane and none into the other. This PR centers it on the line at 2px per side similar to what I see normally (such as VS Code pane), and keeps the highlight on while dragging (previously the highlight disappeared while dragging).

```
[before]
  left │░░░░░ right
       │░░░░░
       1px line + 5px
```

```
[after]
  left ░░│░░ right
       ░░│░░
   2px + 1px line + 2px
```

_Example_ from https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/actions/runs/37401002921/job/112069985119?pr=11506

prs.title: feat(experimental): add an option to cache dependencies instead of statically parsing them
prs.author: sheremet-va
prs.body:
Currently vitest's `--changed` and `related` commands statically parse the module graph to find which tests to run. This PR introduces a new option `experimental.recordDependencies` that keeps a cache of files that ran previously to compare against.

This is significantly (depending on the size of the app) faster if there should be no tests to run since it avoid transform phase entirely.

prs.title: refactor: resolve maxWorkers once in config
prs.author: sheremet-va
prs.body:
`resolveConfig` always sets `maxWorkers` to a number now: percentages, `VITEST_MAX_WORKERS` and the cpu-based default are applied there, and browser instances resolve their own override the same way. The pools, the reporter diagnostics and `doctor` read `config.maxWorkers` directly instead of recomputing the default or falling back to the root config.

The browser pool keeps its 12 pages cap for the default only, using the new `providedOptions.maxWorkers` flag.
